chunks: From him, from Ibn Ribat and Ibn Jabala and Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from al-'Abd al-Salih (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who hires another man for a known wage, and sends him to his estate, and another man gives him dirhams and says to him: 'Buy for me such and such, and whatever profit you make is between me and you.' He (the Imam) said: 'If the one who hired him permits it, there is no harm in it.'

key_terms.فَبَيْنِي وَ بَيْنَكَ: between me and you (indicating shared profit or retention)
key_terms.فَلَيْسَ بِهِ بَأْسٌ: there is no harm in it

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a hired worker keeping profit from a third party's funds?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the permissibility of a hired agent engaging in incidental trade using third-party funds, provided the primary employer grants explicit permission (*idhn*) to retain the surplus profit. It highlights the Shia juristic principle that the validity of such mixed transactions hinges on the employer's consent, distinguishing it from unauthorized agency (*bi-lahib*). This ruling underscores the flexibility in commercial contracts (*ijarah*) when additional benefits are mutually agreed upon.
